transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

I’ve been having trouble keeping my focus at work. Like, I’ll be scheduling appointments or setting up the lobby displays, and I kind of lose my place because I’m worrying I missed something. It’s been bothering me enough that I thought I should come in.
Do you feel anxious when you're worrying about missing something at work?
Yes… I do. It’s not just work, really. I worry about schedules, bills, travel plans, even small paperwork mistakes, like one little mix-up could turn into something bigger.
Do you worry about things outside of work and daily tasks, like your health or relationships?
Some, yeah. It’s mostly ordinary stuff… bills, travel plans, little mistakes on forms. I guess I worry one small thing could turn into a bigger problem.
Do you ever avoid certain tasks or situations because of your worries?
I don’t know… I wouldn’t say I avoid a lot. Maybe I put things off a little if I’m worried I’ll mess them up, but I still usually do them.
Do you experience any physical symptoms like a racing heart, sweating, or trembling when you're worrying?

Not really sweating or trembling, no. It’s more like… I get really tense. Even at the front desk, I can smile and do my job, but inside I feel wound up, like my shoulders are tight and I’m waiting for something to go wrong.
How long have you been experiencing these worries?
About nine months, I think. It kind of started after that overnight detention… and the paperwork mix-up around it. Since then, it’s just been there.
Do you have any thoughts that keep repeating in your mind, even when you try to ignore them?
Yeah… sometimes. I’ll tell myself, like, “Sunny, it’s handled,” but it doesn’t really stop. The thought just keeps going around, and then it turns into checking details in my head over and over.
Do you think your worries are worse than what most people would worry about in the same situations?

Yeah… probably. I know other people worry about bills or work stuff, but I seem to take small things—like a schedule change or a little paperwork mistake—and turn it into something much bigger in my head.
Do you have any thoughts that are intrusive, meaning they come into your mind unwanted and are difficult to control?

Yeah… I guess so. I’ll try to tell myself, “Sunny, it’s handled,” but it keeps looping anyway. Then it kind of jumps from one concern to the next, and I end up checking details in my head over and over.
Have your worries affected your relationships with friends or family?

Not really with friends or family… not that I’ve noticed. It’s more at work. I’m still getting through the day, but scheduling takes me longer because I keep double-checking myself. And sometimes I lose track with the lobby displays and have to redo parts of them.
Have you been avoiding any social activities or hobbies because of your worries?
I don’t think so… not really. I still do the things I usually do. I might be a little slower getting myself to relax, but I haven’t really stopped going anywhere or doing hobbies because of it.
Have your worries significantly impacted your overall quality of life?

Some, yeah. I’m still showing up and getting through the day, so it’s not like everything’s fallen apart. But scheduling takes me longer now because I keep double-checking myself, and with the lobby displays I’ve had to redo parts after I lose track of what I was arranging. So… it’s frustrating.
Do you have thoughts that are intrusive and repetitive, and difficult to stop thinking about?
Yeah… sometimes. I’ll tell myself, “Sunny, it’s handled,” but then the thought keeps coming back. It kind of loops, and then I’m on to the next concern, checking details in my head over and over.
Do you have any thoughts that you feel compelled to repeat over and over in your head?
Yeah… I guess so. Not like a phrase exactly, but I’ll tell myself, “Sunny, it’s handled,” and then it still keeps looping. Then I’m on to another concern, checking the details in my head again.
Do you feel like you have to do certain things over and over, like checking or cleaning, to feel okay or to prevent something bad from happening?
I don’t think so… not in that way. I might double-check things, but I don’t feel like something terrible will happen if I don’t. It’s more just… trying to be sure.
Are your worries mostly about one area of your life, like work, or do they cover a wide range of things?
It’s not just one area, no. It kind of spreads around… work schedules, bills, travel plans, little paperwork mistakes. I’ll start thinking one small mix-up could turn into something bigger.
Have you noticed any significant problems in your personal relationships or daily life outside of work due to your worries?

A little, I guess. I’m still showing up and getting through the day, but some things take me longer now. Like scheduling… I double-check myself a lot. And I’ve had to redo parts of the lobby displays because I lost track of what I was arranging.
Have your worries caused you to feel significantly distressed or overwhelmed on a daily basis?

Yes… I mean, not every moment, but it does get overwhelming some days. I worry about a lot of ordinary things—schedules, bills, travel plans, paperwork—and it’s like one small mistake feels like it could turn into something bigger.
Do you have any thoughts that you feel compelled to think about, even if you don't want to?
Yes… kind of. I can tell myself, “Sunny, it’s handled,” but it doesn’t really stop. The thought just keeps looping, and then I’m onto the next concern, checking the details in my head over and over.
Do you feel like you have to perform certain rituals or behaviors to reduce your anxiety or worries?
I don’t think so… not like rituals. I might check things again if I’m worried, but I wouldn’t say it’s a set thing I have to do.
